questions.question: What is DCAT-US 3.0, and how does it relate to W3C DCAT 3?

kept.text: DCAT-US v3.0 is the federal data catalog metadata standard, updated to improve the Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability (FAIRness) of federal data.
kept.reason: E1 and E3 state this claim verbatim.

kept.text: It is a U.S. application profile of W3C DCAT version 3, not a new or separate standard, so most DCAT-US v3.0 metadata is valid W3C DCAT 3 metadata.
kept.reason: E3 states the profile relation, the not-new-standard point, and the valid-W3C-metadata consequence.
kept.support_span: It is a U.S. application profile of the W3C Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) version 3 - not a new or separate standard. This means most DCAT-US v3.0 metadata is valid W3C DCAT 3 metadata

kept.text: OMB memorandum M-25-05 states the OMB-approved standard metadata schema will conform to the United States profile of the W3C Data Catalog Vocabulary Version 3, known as DCAT-US 3.0.

kept.support_span: The OMB-approved standard metadata schema will conform to the United States profile of the W3C Data Catalog Vocabulary Version 3, known as the DCAT-US 3.0.
